story.title: UAE Suspends All Trade and Financial Transactions with Iran
story.summary: The United Arab Emirates has announced a complete halt to all trade and financial dealings with Iran following the launch of two ballistic missiles from Iran towards the UAE. This decision marks a significant shift in relations, as the UAE has been Iran's most important regional trading partner. The crude oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz has also reportedly decreased to less than a quarter of pre-war levels.

timeline_highlights.summary: Iran has stated that there are no current negotiations or plans for meetings with the United States, contradicting President Trump's assertion of progress in talks that he cited as a reason for canceling planned military strikes. Trump had indicated that discussions regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program were set to occur on the same day he called off the attacks.

timeline_highlights.title: Iran Sets Six Conditions for US to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
timeline_highlights.summary: Iran has outlined six demands that the US must meet to cease attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The exchange of demands has led to rising oil prices and US bond yields, indicating increased market tension.

event_overview.title: About Iran Relations
event_overview.subject: Iran Relations
event_overview.summary: Iran relations in this timeline refers primarily to the adversarial relationship between the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran, where military deterrence, diplomatic contacts, nuclear non-proliferation, sanctions, regional security and maritime transit can interact. The selected developments concern a period in which reported efforts to negotiate or pressure Iran are being weighed alongside threats of force and economic measures affecting Iran and third countries.

facts.label: Diplomatic status
facts.value: The United States and Iran severed diplomatic relations on April 7, 1980, following the November 4, 1979 seizure of the U.S. Embassy in Tehran; the two countries still have no formal diplomatic relationship. Switzerland has served as the U.S. protecting power in Iran since 1980.

facts.label: Sanctions framework
facts.value: U.S. economic restrictions concerning Iran are administered through a combination of statutes, presidential executive orders and Treasury regulations. OFAC describes the program as drawing on authorities including the Iran Sanctions Act, CISADA, CAATSA, IEEPA and regulations in 31 CFR Parts 535, 560, 561 and 562; general licenses can authorize specified activity otherwise prohibited.

facts.label: Nuclear diplomacy
facts.value: The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) was concluded on July 14, 2015 by Iran, China, France, Germany, Russia, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union, and was endorsed by UN Security Council Resolution 2231 on July 20, 2015. The UN states that, effective September 27, 2025, earlier Iran-related Security Council resolutions were re-applied under Resolution 2231's process.

facts.label: International nuclear safeguards
facts.value: Iran's safeguards agreement with the International Atomic Energy Agency in connection with the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty entered into force on May 15, 1974. The IAEA lists an Additional Protocol signed by Iran on December 18, 2003, separately from the safeguards agreement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the immediate diplomacy, coercive economic measures and regional trade or maritime pressures associated with this episode; it does not attempt to cover the full history of U.S.-Iran relations, every sanctions action, or all nuclear and regional-security developments.

related_stories.summary: Australia's foreign minister has summoned the Israeli ambassador in response to Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the death of an Australian aid worker during a 2024 airstrike in Gaza. The minister described the decision as 'insulting' and expressed the nation's outrage over the matter.

related_stories.title: Intense Russian Bombardment in Kyiv Results in Multiple Casualties
related_stories.summary: A significant Russian missile and drone attack on Kyiv has resulted in at least 12 to 16 fatalities and numerous injuries. The bombardment, described as one of the heaviest since the war began, targeted residential areas, including a children's hospital and schools. The strikes caused extensive damage to buildings and disrupted power supply in parts of the city.

related_stories.title: North Korea Launches Up to 10 Ballistic Missiles Amid U.S.-South Korea Military Drills
related_stories.summary: North Korea has launched more than 10 short-range ballistic missiles into the sea, coinciding with President Trump's announcement of scaled-back military drills with South Korea. The South Korean presidential office condemned the missile launches and ordered military readiness during ongoing joint exercises with the U.S. Reports indicate that the missiles landed outside Japan's exclusive economic zone.
